source_title: Dragon Ball Z: 5 Best Movies in the Series, Ranked
source_excerpt:
Renan is the Anime Lead Editor for GameRant. Ren graduated Cum Laude from Lesley University in 2017 and has been focusing exclusively on his journalistic endeavors ever since. When Ren isn't working, he's usually playing video games or reading.
Dragon Ball Z is one of the greatest anime of all time. An adaptation of Volumes 17 through 42 of Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball manga, DBZ redefined what it meant to be a shonen anime while influencing genres and mediums worldwide. Although Dragon Ball Z is best known as an anime these days, the series had its fair share of movies while Toei was still adapting Toriyama's masterpiece.
The Dragon Ball Z films often varied in quality, but the best of the best were as good as anything Akira Toriyama came up with himself. The greatest DBZ movies in the series stand alongside the anime's greatest sagas, offering everything fans love most about the original manga and anime.
5 Broly – The Legendary Super Saiyan Contains Some of the Highest Highs in Dragon Ball
Super Saiyan Goku vs Broly The Legendary Super Saiyan Dragon Ball Z
Super Saiyan Goku vs Broly The Legendary Super Saiyan Dragon Ball Z
Broly – The Legendary Super Saiyan gets a bad rep these days, but the movie has aged better than most films in the series. The first Broly movie was the only feature-length Dragon Ball Z movie before Battle of Gods , and its artistic ambition extends well beyond its story. This is one of the best directed movies in the series, featuring amazingly intense fight choreography, beautiful shot composition, and striking coloring.
While Dragon Ball Super: Broly is a straightforward improvement over The Legendary Super Saiyan , there's something to appreciate about DBZ Movie 8's more epic take on Broly. The film really feels like a natural consequence of everything we've learned about Saiyan lore throughout the Dragon Ball Z anime. How Goku beats Broly doesn't feel particularly earned, but the rest of the movie is nothing short of fantastic if you can meet it on its level.
4 Fusion Reborn is Just Pure Fun From Top to Bottom
Dragon Ball Z: Fusion Reborn is one of the most fun movies in the series. The film is basically an excuse for the animators to flex their talents while also getting a chance to bring back a ton of fan favorite villains, including Frieza. Fusion Reborn understands that most fans are just here for the action and immediately indulges in it. Goku, Vegeta, Gotenks, and Gohan all get some great fights, and the dark borders around characters give the film a visual identity the other DBZ movies don't have.
Of course, the highlight of the movie is Gogeta's battle with Janemba, but there's a surprisingly deep emotional core at the heart of the story. Goku and Vegeta's relationship plays a key role in the plot, with Fusion Reborn 's ending acting as a profound goodbye to their rivalry and relationship. For a movie that exists primarily to set up fights, the fact Fusion Reborn has one of the saddest scenes in the franchise really elevates it into a masterpiece.
3 Cooler's Revenge Has the Best Super Saiyan Transformation in the Series
Dragon Ball Z: Cooler's Revenge is actually canon to the Dragon Ball Z anime, taking place in-between the Future Trunks Saga and the start of the Androids Saga. Set during the three-year gap for the battle with Dr. Gero, Cooler ends up coming to Earth for revenge against Goku. Cooler's Revenge is ultimately a soft remake of the Frieza Saga, but excellent art direction, a beautiful backdrop for the film, and Cooler's raw charisma give the film a lot of charm.
This is also one of the few movies in the series to give Piccolo plenty of great moments (including the film's final kill), as well as the best animated and directed Super Saiyan transformation in the franchise. Goku triggering SSJ and reviving a bird so that he can destroy Cooler and propel him into the sun with a Kamehameha is downright inspired. Cooler's final form also has a brilliant design, giving him a menacing edge over Frieza. If the movie weren't so derivative, Cooler's Revenge would be right up there with Battle of Gods and DBS: Broly .
2 The Dead Zone is a Perfect Balance of OG Dragon Ball & DBZ
The very first DBZ movie, Dragon Ball Z: The Dead Zone exists in one of the most interesting periods in Dragon Ball history – the original series had just ended, but Dragon Ball Z hadn't become the intensely dramatic sci-fi anime fans would come to know it as. The Dead Zone features the trademark action that made DBZ so compelling, but with all of the original Dragon Ball 's mysticism and spiritualism.
The end result is an incredibly unique movie with beautiful art direction and stellar fight choreography. Notably, The Dead Zone marks one of the last times Goku would use the Power Pole in combat. While the story is mainly a remake of the Raditz battle, the extra lore for Kami and the Dead Zone are so distinct that it hardly feels like a repeat of the Saiyan Saga. If it weren't for Krillin meeting Gohan, you could even consider The Dead Zone canon.
1 Battle of Gods Has The Best Story of Any DBZ Movie
Beerus punches Goku in the face in Dragon Ball Super. Image vua Toei Animation
Beerus prepares a special Hakai blast in Dragon Ball Z: Battle of the Gods. Image via Toei Animation
What Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods lacks in art direction and animation, it makes up for by having the best writing of any Dragon Ball movie, period. Battle of Gods was the first Dragon Ball movie written by Akira Toriyama himself, and the difference in quality between it and the thirteen original DBZ films is absolutely staggering. Battle of Gods has legitimate thematic depth, great character arcs for Goku & Vegeta, and a story that serves as a symbolic second ending for the series.
Battle of Gods ended up being so popular that it single-handedly revived the series and led to the creation of Dragon Ball Super . Battle of Gods feels like a true episode to Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball manga, serving as a love letter to Goku, Vegeta, and all the minor characters who made the series popular. Super Saiyan God Goku's battle with Beerus is a highlight, but it's the little moments – like Goku, Bulma, and Oolong reuniting for the final scene for one last gag – that elevates BoG . It's not just a good Dragon Ball Z movie, it's a great anime movie.
